subject: maths
title: Coordinates and Transformations: Translate, Reflect and Rotate
seo_title: Year 5 Coordinates and Transformations Worksheets: Translations, Reflections, Rotations and Symmetry (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations of shapes, using dynamic geometric software where appropriate; recognise what changes and what remains the same, and identify any symmetries
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on coordinates and transformations for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5SP03, AC9M5SP02): read and plot coordinates, translate, reflect and rotate shapes on a grid, and find line and rotational symmetry. 100 questions with an answer key, good NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Translate = slide, reflect = flip, rotate = turn. The shape stays the same size.
key_sub: Coordinates: across first, then up. Count squares, not lines. A quarter turn clockwise turns right into down; a reflection lands the same distance on the other side of the mirror line.
body_html:
Coordinates: across, then up

A coordinate grid has a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis. They meet at the origin, (0, 0). Coordinates like (4, 5) tell you to go across first, then up.

On a map grid with north up the page, east and west change the x-coordinate, and north and south change the y-coordinate.

Translations: slide the shape

A translation slides a shape left or right and up or down. Every corner moves the same number of squares in the same direction.

MoveWhat changesExample from (5, 4)
right 2x gets bigger(7, 4)
left 2x gets smaller(3, 4)
up 2y gets bigger(5, 6)
down 2y gets smaller(5, 2)
Example 1

Describe the translation from (2, 7) to (8, 3).

Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down.

Answer: 6 squares right and 4 squares down

Reflections: flip in a mirror line

A reflection flips a shape over a mirror line. Each corner ends up the same distance from the line, on the other side. The line x = 5 is vertical; the line y = 4 is horizontal.

Example 2

Reflect (3, 4) in the mirror line x = 5.

(3, 4) is 2 squares left of the line. Go 2 squares right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4.

Answer: (7, 4)

Rotations: turn about a point

A rotation turns a shape about a fixed point, the centre of rotation. A quarter turn is 90°, a half turn is 180°. Clockwise is the way the hands of a clock go; anticlockwise is the other way.

TurnRight becomesUp becomes
quarter turn clockwisedownright
quarter turn anticlockwiseupleft
half turnleftdown

What changes and what stays the same

After a translation, reflection or rotation the shape is in a new place, but it is the same shape and size. Side lengths, angles, perimeter and area stay the same. A reflection faces the other way; a rotation is turned.

A shape has line symmetry if it can be folded so the two halves match exactly. It has rotational symmetry if it fits onto its outline before a full turn. A square has 4 lines of symmetry and fits onto itself 4 times in a full turn (order 4). A rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry: the diagonals are not lines of symmetry.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping x and y: (2, 5) plotted as 5 across, 2 upAcross first, then up
Counting grid lines, starting with 1 on the start lineCount the squares you jump
Reflecting by sliding: the image points the same wayFlip it: the image must face the other way
Turning the wrong way, or a half turn instead of a quarter turnClockwise: right becomes down. A quarter turn is 90°
Thinking the shape gets bigger or smallerCheck every side is the same length as before

faq.q: What do Year 5 students learn about transformations in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: In Year 5 (AC9M5SP03) students describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations of shapes, recognise what changes and what stays the same, and identify symmetries. They also use grid coordinates and directional language to describe position and movement (AC9M5SP02).

faq.q: What is the difference between a translation, a reflection and a rotation?
faq.a: A translation slides a shape, so it still faces the same way. A reflection flips it in a mirror line, and a rotation turns it about a point.

faq.q: How do you rotate a shape a quarter turn clockwise?
faq.a: Keep the centre of rotation still and turn the shape 90° the way clock hands move, so a side that pointed right now points down. Tracing paper helps: trace the shape, hold the centre with a pencil and turn.

faq.q: Does a shape change size when it is translated, reflected or rotated?
faq.a: No. Only its position and the way it faces can change. The side lengths, angles, perimeter and area stay exactly the same.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 3 on the x-axis, then up to 5. Point C is at (3, 5). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 6 on the x-axis, then up to 2. Point B is at (6, 2). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 1 on the x-axis, then up to 4. Point A is at (1, 4). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 7 on the x-axis, then up to 6. Point B is at (7, 6). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 4 and do not go up at all: the point is on the x-axis. Point A is at (4, 0). The x-coordinate is written first.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 2 on the x-axis, then up to 5. The point is at (2, 5). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point C.

items.q: Which point is at (6, 3)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 6 on the x-axis, then up to 3. The point is at (6, 3). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point B.

items.q: Which point is at (5, 7)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across to 5 on the x-axis, then up to 7. The point is at (5, 7). Across first, then up: the x-coordinate is written first. That is point A.

items.q: Which point is at (0, 6)?
items.e: x = 0 means you do not go across at all. Go straight up the y-axis to 6. That is point D. (6, 0) is on the x-axis instead.

items.q: In the coordinates (3, 7), which number tells you how far to go across?
items.e: The first number is the x-coordinate: how far across. The second number is the y-coordinate: how far up. (3, 7) is 3 across and 7 up.

items.q: What is the point (0, 0) called?
items.e: (0, 0) is where the x-axis and the y-axis meet. It is called the origin. You start counting from there.

items.q: Which point is on the y-axis?
items.e: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0, because you do not go across. (6, 0) is on the x-axis.

items.q: On a map grid of a school excursion to the zoo, north is up the page. William starts at (1, 2) and walks 3 squares east and 2 squares north to the koala enclosure. What are the coordinates of the koala enclosure?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. East 3 squares changes x: 1 + 3 = 4. North 2 squares changes y: 2 + 2 = 4. The new point is (4, 4).

items.q: On a map grid of a school camp, north is up the page. Aarav starts at (7, 6) and walks 4 squares west and 3 squares south to the dining hall. What are the coordinates of the dining hall?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. West 4 squares changes x: 7 − 4 = 3. South 3 squares changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (3, 3).

items.q: On a map grid of the botanic gardens, north is up the page. Mei starts at (2, 8) and walks 5 squares east and 6 squares south to the lily pond. What are the coordinates of the lily pond?
items.e: East and west change x; north and south change y. East 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. South 6 squares changes y: 8 − 6 = 2. The new point is (7, 2).

items.q: Jack is at (4, 6) on a map grid where north is up. His friend is at (4, 2). In which direction should he walk to reach his friend?
items.e: x stays 4, so there is no move east or west. y goes from 6 down to 2, which is down the page: south.

items.q: On a map grid of a school, north is up the page. The canteen is at (2, 3) and the library is at (7, 3). How do you walk from the canteen to the library?
items.e: y stays 3, so there is no move north or south. x goes from 2 up to 7: 7 − 2 = 5 squares to the right, which is east. Count squares, not lines (that gives 6).

items.q: A rectangle has three corners at (1, 1), (6, 1) and (6, 4). What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
items.e: The fourth corner is above (1, 1) and across from (6, 4). So it has x-coordinate 1 and y-coordinate 4: (1, 4).

items.q: How many squares apart are the points (2, 6) and (9, 6)?
items.e: The y-coordinates are the same, so the points are on the same row. Take the x-coordinates: 9 − 2 = 7 squares. Counting the lines, including the first one, gives 8.

items.q: Lachlan wants to plot the point (2, 5). He goes 5 across and then 2 up. What mistake did he make?
c: He should go down, not up
items.e: Across first, then up. (2, 5) means 2 across and 5 up. Lachlan plotted (5, 2) instead.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 squares right. Up and down: 3 to 1 is 2 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 2) and B is at (3, 6). Across: 6 to 3 is 3 squares left. Up and down: 2 to 6 is 4 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (3, 6) and B is at (3, 1). The x-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 6 to 1 is 5 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (1, 1) moves to (6, 5) in B. That is 5 squares right and 4 squares up. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one corner. The corner of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 squares left and 4 squares down. Every corner moves the same way.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (2, 7) to (8, 3). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (8, 3). Across: 2 to 8 is 6 squares right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 squares down. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: A corner of a shape moves from (9, 1) to (5, 6). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (9, 1) and the end is at (5, 6). Across: 9 to 5 is 4 squares left. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 squares up. Count the squares you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It is translated 2 squares right and 3 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 2 squares changes x: 3 + 2 = 5. Up 3 squares changes y: 4 + 3 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 7). It is translated 5 squares right and 4 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 squares changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Down 4 squares changes y: 7 − 4 = 3. The new point is (7, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (8, 3). It is translated 6 squares left and 2 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 6 squares changes x: 8 − 6 = 2. Up 2 squares changes y: 3 + 2 = 5. The new point is (2, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (1, 2). It is translated 6 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays 1. Up 6 squares changes y: 2 + 6 = 8. The new point is (1, 8).

items.q: Point P is translated 4 squares right and 3 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 4 squares changes x: 2 + 4 = 6. Down 3 squares changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (6, 3). That is point D.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 squares left and 4 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 5 squares changes x: 7 − 5 = 2. Up 4 squares changes y: 2 + 4 = 6. The new point is (2, 6). That is point A.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 squares right and 5 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 6 squares changes x: 1 + 6 = 7. Up 5 squares changes y: 1 + 5 = 6. The new point is (7, 6). That is point C.

items.q: A triangle has corners at (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 3). It is translated 3 squares right and 4 squares up. Which list shows the new corners?
items.e: Add 3 to every x-coordinate and 4 to every y-coordinate: (2, 1) → (5, 5), (5, 1) → (8, 5), (2, 3) → (5, 7). Move every corner, not just one.

items.q: Point B is translated 4 squares right and 3 squares up. It lands on (6, 8). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards and undo each move. 4 right is undone by 4 left: 6 − 4 = 2. 3 up is undone by 3 down: 8 − 3 = 5. B started at (2, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 4) and point B is at (6, 4). Zara counts the grid lines from A to B, starting with 1 on A’s line, and says A moved 5 right. What is the correct translation?
items.e: Count the squares you jump, not the lines: 6 − 2 = 4. Zara counted the line A starts on, so she got 1 too many.

items.q: Liam translates (6, 4) 2 squares left and gets (8, 4). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Moving left makes the x-coordinate smaller: 6 − 2 = 4. The correct answer is (4, 4). Liam added 2, which is a move to the right.

items.q: A point is translated up or down. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: Up and down is the y direction. The point does not move left or right, so the x-coordinate stays the same.

sets.title: Reflections in a vertical or horizontal line

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical mirror line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal mirror line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal mirror line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 squares above the line y = 6. The image is 3 squares below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal mirror line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 squares below the line y = 5. The image is 2 squares above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 squares to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 squares to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 squares to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point C: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 squares below the line y = 3. The image is 2 squares above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the mirror line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 squares above the line y = 4. The image is 2 squares below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 square too far (the lines were counted, starting with 1 on the line P is on). Point B: it stops on the mirror line. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same row. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image has more squares, so its size changed; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way); C: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same column. Only C is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way); D: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same row. Only B is a true mirror image. Others: A: the image has more squares, so its size changed; C: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it points the same way); D: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed mirror line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each blue square must be the same number of squares from the mirror line as its green partner, on the other side, in the same column. Only A is a true mirror image. Others: B: the shape was turned upside down, not flipped; C: the image is 1 square too far from the mirror line; D: the image has more squares, so its size changed.

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the vertical mirror line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is on the mirror line x = 5, so it does not move: (5, 3). A point on the mirror line is its own reflection.

items.q: A point is reflected in a vertical mirror line. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: A vertical mirror line goes up and down. The point flips across it, left to right, so only x changes. y stays the same.

items.q: Point P is 3 squares to the left of a vertical mirror line. Where is its image?
c: 4 squares to the right of the line
3 squares to the right of the line
3 squares to the left of the line
6 squares to the right of the line
items.e: In a reflection the image is the same distance from the mirror line as the point, on the other side.

items.q: Sienna reflects a right-angled triangle in a vertical mirror line. Her image points the same way as the triangle. What mistake did she make?
c: She slid it instead of flipping it
items.e: A reflection is a mirror image, so it faces the other way. If the image points the same way, the shape was slid (translated).

items.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 5), (1, 5). It is reflected in the vertical mirror line x = 4. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (1, 5)?
items.e: The corner (1, 5) is 3 squares to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 squares to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 5. The image is (7, 5).

items.q: A triangle has corners at (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 2). It is reflected in the horizontal mirror line y = 3. Which list shows the corners of the image?
items.e: Each corner goes the same distance on the other side of y = 3, and x stays the same. (2, 1) is 2 below the line, so it goes to (2, 5). (2, 2) is 1 below, so it goes to (2, 4).

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (4, 5), P (7, 5) is 3 right. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 3 down from O: (4, 2). That is point C. Point A: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point B: turned a half turn. Point D: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (5, 3), P (5, 6) is 3 up. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So the image is 3 right from O: (8, 3). That is point D. Point A: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point B: turned a half turn. Point C: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Point P is rotated a quarter turn anticlockwise about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (4, 5), P (6, 6) is 2 right, 1 up. In a quarter turn anticlockwise, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So the image is 1 left, 2 up from O: (3, 7). That is point A. Point B: turned a quarter turn clockwise. Point C: turned a half turn. Point D: flipped in a mirror line, not turned.

items.q: Point P is rotated a half turn about point O. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: From O (5, 4), P (7, 6) is 2 right, 2 up. In a half turn, right turns into left and up turns into down. So the image is 2 left, 2 down from O: (3, 2). That is point B. Point A: turned a quarter turn clockwise. Point C: turned a quarter turn anticlockwise. Point D: turned the right way, but 1 square too far from O.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (5, 1) and points down. Right to down is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (4, 7) and points up. In B the matching side goes to (1, 4) and points left. Up to left is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (2, 4) and points left. Right to left is a half turn.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A in the vertical line through O: every corner stays at the same height, for example (7, 6) → (3, 6). A turn about O would keep the shape the same way round; this one is flipped.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (4, 6) and points up. In B the matching side goes to (7, 3) and points right. Up to right is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Point O does not move. What happened to shape A?
items.e: Follow the side that starts at O. In A it goes from O to (8, 4) and points right. In B the matching side goes to (5, 7) and points up. Right to up is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: The green shape is turned a quarter turn clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot stays still and the shape turns around it. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. Follow the part of the shape that touches the dot. Only A is correct, and the shape is still the same size. Others: B: it was turned anticlockwise; C: it was turned a half turn; D: it was flipped in a mirror line, not turned.

items.q: The green shape is turned a quarter turn anticlockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot stays still and the shape turns around it. In a quarter turn anticlockwise, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. Follow the part of the shape that touches the dot. Only C is correct, and the shape is still the same size. Others: A: it was turned a half turn; B: it was turned clockwise; D: it was flipped upside down, not turned.

items.q: The green shape is turned a half turn about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot stays still and the shape turns around it. In a half turn, right turns into left and up turns into down. Follow the part of the shape that touches the dot. Only D is correct, and the shape is still the same size. Others: A: it was turned clockwise; B: it was flipped in a mirror line, not turned; C: it was turned anticlockwise.

items.q: The green shape is turned a quarter turn clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot stays still and the shape turns around it. In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. Follow the part of the shape that touches the dot. Only B is correct, and the shape is still the same size. Others: A: it was flipped upside down, not turned; C: it was turned a half turn; D: it was turned anticlockwise.

items.q: P is 3 squares to the right of O. P is rotated a quarter turn clockwise about O. Where is P now?
c: 3 squares to the left of O
items.e: In a quarter turn clockwise, right turns into down, like the hand of a clock going from 3 to 6. P stays the same distance from O: 3 squares below O.

items.q: P is 2 squares above O. P is rotated a half turn about O. Where is P now?
c: 2 squares to the right of O
2 squares to the left of O
items.e: A half turn turns up into down. P stays the same distance from O, so it is 2 squares below O, not 4.

items.q: P is 4 squares to the left of O. P is rotated a quarter turn anticlockwise about O. Where is P now?
c: 4 squares to the right of O
items.e: Anticlockwise goes the other way to the hands of a clock: left turns into down (from 9 back to 6). P is still 4 squares from O.

items.q: Mia faces north. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face now?
items.e: Clockwise goes north → east → south → west. A quarter turn is one step: east.

items.q: P is 2 squares to the right of O. Harper rotates P a quarter turn clockwise about O and puts it 2 squares above O. What mistake did she make?
c: She moved it too far from O
She turned it a half turn
items.e: Clockwise turns right into down, so P should be 2 squares below O. Going from right to up is a quarter turn anticlockwise.

items.q: The point (6, 3) is rotated a half turn about the point (4, 3). What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (6, 3) is 2 squares right of (4, 3). A half turn turns right into left, so the image is 2 squares left: (2, 3). It does not stop on the centre.

sets.title: What stays the same, symmetry and problems

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every corner moved 5 squares right and 3 squares up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4).

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A in the line x = 5: (1, 1) → (9, 1) and (4, 1) → (6, 1). The shape is flipped but the same size.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is A turned a quarter turn clockwise about the corner (4, 1): the side from (4, 1) to (1, 1) pointed left and now points up, to (4, 4). The shape is the same size.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: The bottom side of A is 3 squares long, but the bottom side of B is 6 squares long. B is bigger, so it is not a translation, a reflection or a rotation.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this rectangle have?
items.e: A rectangle has only 2 lines of symmetry, through the middles of opposite sides. The diagonals are not lines of symmetry: if you fold along a diagonal, the corners do not meet.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this equilateral triangle have?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, so it has 3 lines of symmetry, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this parallelogram have?
items.e: A parallelogram has no lines of symmetry. If you fold it in half either way, the halves do not match, because the sides slope.

items.q: How many lines of symmetry does this kite have?
items.e: A kite has 1 line of symmetry, through the corners where the equal sides meet.

items.q: Turn this square about its centre. How many times does it fit exactly onto its outline in one full turn?
items.e: Turn a tracing of the shape. The square fits onto its outline 4 times in one full turn (every 90°), so it has rotational symmetry of order 4. Count the full turn once, not the start as well.

items.q: This pinwheel pattern is turned about its centre. How many times does it fit exactly onto its outline in one full turn?
items.e: Turn a tracing of the shape. The pinwheel fits onto its outline 4 times in one full turn (every 90°), so it has rotational symmetry of order 4. Count the full turn once, not the start as well.

items.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
items.e: The parallelogram (D) fits onto itself after a half turn, but folding it never makes the halves match. The rectangle has both kinds of symmetry. The kite and the isosceles triangle have a line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry.

items.q: A stop sign is shaped like a regular octagon. How many lines of symmetry does a regular octagon have?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 lines of symmetry: 4 through opposite corners and 4 through the middles of opposite sides.

items.q: The cells in a honeycomb are shaped like regular hexagons. How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 lines of symmetry: 3 through opposite corners and 3 through the middles of opposite sides.

items.q: A give way sign is shaped like an equilateral triangle. The triangle is turned about its centre. How many times does it fit exactly onto its outline in one full turn?
items.e: The triangle fits onto its outline after one third of a turn, two thirds of a turn and the full turn: 3 times. It has rotational symmetry of order 3.

items.q: Ruby draws a triangle with a 50° angle on a grid and rotates it a quarter turn. What is the size of that angle in the image?
items.e: A rotation turns the shape but does not change it. Every angle stays the same, so the angle is still 50°. The 90° is how far the shape turned, not an angle of the triangle.

items.q: On a playground plan, a rectangular sandpit is 4 m long and 3 m wide. It is rotated a half turn. What is the perimeter of the image?
items.e: A rotation does not change the side lengths. The perimeter is still 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 = 14 m. (12 is the area in square metres.)

items.q: Charlotte rotates a shape a quarter turn. She says the image is smaller because it has been turned. Is she right?
c: No: a rotation never changes the size
Yes, but only for a quarter turn
items.e: After a translation, a reflection or a rotation the shape is the same size, with the same side lengths and angles. Only its position, and the way it faces, can change.

items.q: A shape is rotated a quarter turn about one of its corners. Which of these changes?
items.e: A rotation turns the shape, so it faces a new way (and most of it moves). The size, angles and side lengths stay the same.

items.q: In a coding lesson, a robot is at (5, 3) on a grid and faces north (up the page). It turns a quarter turn clockwise, then moves 3 squares forward. Where is it now?
items.e: A quarter turn clockwise from north is east, which is to the right. 3 squares east changes x: 5 + 3 = 8. The robot is at (8, 3).

items.q: A tile in a floor pattern is turned a quarter turn clockwise, 3 times. Which single turn ends in the same place?
items.e: 3 quarter turns clockwise is a three-quarter turn. A full turn is 4 quarter turns, so it is 1 quarter turn short of a full turn: the same as a quarter turn the other way, anticlockwise.
